confirmed.statement: Per-arm counts at assignment are not printed. Subtraction gives 35 / 33 / 32, so the null per-arm n_randomized follows form-spec rule 1.

In Table S3, the 'Achieved Power (n=97)' row sits in the 'Post-hoc Power Analysis' block, below the 'Intent-to-Treat Analysis' block. Power 0.554 reproduces at N = 97 with f = 0.244 (checker arithmetic: 0.552 at 97, 0.538 at 94, 0.566 at 100). The ITT block's Observed F = 2.720 with eta-squared 0.0564 fits 91 residual df (94 observations), a source inconsistency beside the form's open question on F = 2.33 versus 2.720. No passage states an analyzed count other than 97.

Checker arithmetic confirms the form's open question on Tables 5-6. Among all group sizes up to 100 (Table 5) and 60 (Table 6), only 41 / 56 and 27 / 29 give whole totals for the six count variables and reproduce all 14 printed t-statistics within 0.0013. The assigned 32 / 65 and 33 / 32 fail both checks. The form keeps these groups out of the people counts (n_units null, statistics_available test_statistic only).
S1 (Phase 1) has no people. Its units are 300 persona plots and 30 benchmark plots, and the form codes its people counts null, counts_are 'other' and population empty.

No shared sample. S2 is the paper's only study with people, and it is a new Prolific sample. Doshi and Hauser's 293 writers appear only as reprinted estimates (Table 2) and in a power comparison (p. 15). The c006 form also treats c128 as its own sample, and no other candidate matches Wan and Kalman or arXiv 2504.13868. The paper does not say whether earlier Doshi and Hauser workers were screened out.

confirmed.statement: Population, who and country match the source: UK-based Prolific workers with approval at or above 95 percent and 100 to 1,000,000 prior submissions, over 18, paid 3 pounds for about 15-20 minutes.
Criterion 2 holds for S2 alone: 97 people analyzed across three arms. Each AI-versus-control contrast still has 65 (1-plot) or 64 (5-plot) people.

summary: The people counts hold: S2 randomized 100 UK Prolific workers, dropped 3 control writers who reported using GenAI, and analyzed 97 people (32 / 33 / 32, one story each), so S2 alone meets the 50-person criterion and shares no sample with another study or paper. The form already flags the weak spots (per-arm assignment counts not printed, a control-only exclusion, Tables 5-6 built on 41 / 56 and 27 / 29 stories), and the one new finding is a source inconsistency: Table S3's F and eta-squared imply 94 observations, while every printed count is 97.
